title: Counter-Positioning
coreMove: Find the business-model move that improves the entrant while making imitation painful for the incumbent.
sourcePressure: Counter-positioning means a newcomer adopts a superior business model the incumbent will not mimic because copying would damage the existing business. The pressure is the incumbent trap, not novelty for its own sake.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Counter-positioning means being disruptive, cheaper, digital, or more innovative in a loose sense.

sourceAnchors.name: Scylla and Charybdis
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar says the subtitle supports the incumbent being trapped between painful options
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The incumbent is not blind; it is caught between copying the entrant and injuring the business that still pays the bills.
